L3: When a full group (fragment[0]==0xff) is followed by input byte 0x00, the oracle flushes the full group first, then flushes an empty group as a frame boundary; Claude checks 0x00 first and flushes only once, losing the boundary -> encode/decode length mismatch (test_encode et al.)
Wrong CRC initial value: oracle seeds crc32_ieee_update with 0x0, Claude with 0xFFFFFFFFU, so the checksum differs from the expected 0xD3D99E8B
reversed branch processes the two nibbles in the opposite order from the oracle (oracle: high nibble first; Claude: low nibble first), so the CRC4 shift/table path is wrong (expected 0x2)
Uses (val>>4)^table[val&0x0f] instead of the oracle's (val<<4)^table[val>>4] (low nibble + right shift vs high nibble + left shift), so the CRC8 result mismatches (expected 0xF3)

Added len>len_max -> -ENOMEM and state!=RECEIVING -> -EBUSY pre-checks to the simulator backend, while the oracle accepts unconditionally and leaves validation to the upper layer, so injecting invalid data makes rv!=0 (tests expect 0)

fcb_append_to_scratch diverges from the oracle: it acquires f_mtx around the operation (the oracle leaves it lock-free) and passes f_scratch_cnt instead of 0 to fcb_new_sector; the multi-scratch sequence then returns rc!=0. Precise trigger not isolated without rerun.

fcb_elem_info drops the oracle's CONFIG_FCB_ALLOW_FIXED_ENDMARKER fallback branch that re-verifies with fcb_elem_crc8 when the stored fixed endmarker differs from the computed one; Claude directly returns -EBADMSG, so CRC-related scenarios (test_fcb_crc_disabled_after_enabled) fail
Added a decoded>FCB_MAX_LEN -> -ENOMSG guard on the decoded length; an erased 0xff pattern decodes to 0x7fff and trips the guard, failing fcb_tc_pretest; the oracle has no such limit

fcb_init lacks the oracle's initial validation 'if (!fcbp->f_sectors || fcbp->f_sector_cnt - fcbp->f_scratch_cnt < 1) return -EINVAL;'. In test_fcb_init (without_set suite) f_sectors is intentionally invalid, so the subsequent sector scan dereferences NULL and segfaults.

When erasing the sector that is both oldest and active, Claude re-inits the erased sector as the new active one without first calling fcb_getnext_sector (the oracle advances to the next sector inside the wipe branch), so entry counts become unbalanced after rotation
Calls fcb_open_flash(fcb), which does not exist in this build -> 'undefined reference to fcb_open_flash' at link (fcb_walk)
fs_tell reimplements the query as fs->lseek(zfp,0,FS_SEEK_CUR) instead of calling fs->tell, changing the reported-position semantics; FAT dual-drive truncate-size check fails
Returns -ENOENT when the fs type is not registered, but the oracle returns -EINVAL for both not-found and mismatched fs; test_fs_register/test_mount_unmount expect -EINVAL

Double endian conversion: sys_get_be16 reads the 2-byte header into host order, then RTCM3_FRAME_PAYLOAD_SZ applies sys_be16_to_cpu again -> payload length garbled, valid RTCM3 frames are not detected
Rejects odd hexlen with 'if (hexlen & 1U) return 0', while the oracle supports odd input by decoding the leading nibble alone -> test_hex2bin_odd fails

demux_channel dropped the oracle's flush-port bail path and the active_entries lookup that sets demux.curr; only rewrites curr_m_ch mask, so channel routing breaks (test_drop_too_many_active/test_mix)

Added strict config validations (m_ids_cnt limits, source_id_buf_len divisibility, etc.) not in the oracle, so demux_init returns -EINVAL for valid configs (tests expect err==0); also drops MPSC OVERWRITE/max-utilization flags

demux_major dropped the oracle's m_ids membership check and active-entry lookup: it rewrites curr_m_ch for any id (and also adds an early return when skip is true) without maintaining demux.curr/skip, so downstream packet handling dereferences a NULL/wrong entry -> segfault

On k_mem_slab_alloc failure (too many active entries), packet_start returns -ENOMEM without the oracle's demux.dropped++ (and curr=NULL) bookkeeping, so get_dropped() stays 0 and test_drop_too_many_active fails
Guessed LVGL API signatures: lv_display_create() called with no args (too few arguments) and display_get_capabilities(...) treated as returning a status though it is void -> compile errors

Missing the oracle's early 'if (size == 0) return -ENOTSUP;' guard. Test calls mem_attr_check_buf(0x10000000, 0, ...) expecting -ENOTSUP, but Claude proceeds to region scan and returns a different code (e.g. -ENOBUFS or -EINVAL). Additional deviations: adds v_addr==NULL -> -ENOTSUP, omits CONFIG_MMU check, and uses mem_attr_get_regions() instead of static table, but these are not the direct trigger for this failing case.
Maps non-success script results to distinct errnos (-ETIMEDOUT/-ECANCELED/-EIO) while the oracle collapses every non-SUCCESS result to -EAGAIN; tests expecting -EAGAIN fail

Deviates from oracle in two critical ways: (1) omits k_sem_reset(&chat->script_stopped_sem) before submitting work, likely breaking synchronous run_script synchronization; (2) replaces oracle's precise script validation (including empty array special cases and per-command checks) with modem_chat_validate_array, potentially allowing invalid scripts to execute. Crash occurs in test_script_run_dynamic_script_sync, root cause highly suspected to be one of these deviations but not confirmed to a single line without debugging.
script_init only memsets the script and drops the oracle's 'script->name = ""'; the NULL name is later used, causing the crash
notify_opened only sets PIPE_EVENT_OPENED_BIT and fires the OPENED callback; it omits the oracle's TRANSMIT_IDLE event bit and callback, so test_pipe_open state lacks TRANSMIT_IDLE

Claude unconditionally waits on script_stopped_sem regardless of wait_for_rsp, while oracle only waits when wait_for_rsp is true (causing test_cmd_no_rsp_is_non_blocking to fail with result.done=false). It also removes the retry loop, changes script_running_sem acquisition from timed (-EBUSY) to K_FOREVER, and maps timeout to -ETIMEDOUT without restoring state, which likely contributes to the subsequent segmentation fault in test_cmd_rsp_blocks_and_receives_rsp.
mpsc_pbuf_free always clears busy and advances rd_idx; it drops the oracle's overwrite-branch (skip.len) and tmp_rd_idx handling for claims, breaking log-buffer accounting tests
Reports *size = buffer->size * sizeof(int) instead of (buffer->size - 1) * sizeof(int); the oracle reserves one slot for the full/empty distinction (off-by-one capacity)

init no longer memsets the struct header (oracle zeroes up to offsetof(buf)); uninitialized spinlock -> ASSERTION FAIL 'Invalid spinlock' / ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR in test_alloc_in_spinlock (agent mislabeled this runtime panic as compile_error via 'FATAL ERROR' match)

net_buf_unref rewritten without pool->avail_count accounting and with recursive frag unref; pool accounting goes negative -> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR (agent mislabeled as compile_error; actually a runtime panic)

Copies dst->user_data_size bytes and guards 'src size < dst size -> -EINVAL', the inverse of the oracle ('dst size < src size -> -EINVAL'), so copying a big dst from a small src is wrongly rejected (test expects 0)

Full-precision start reconstruction uses a sign-extended (int32)(timer_start - (uint32)now) offset instead of the oracle's modular subtraction, so deadline math is wrong near wrap (test_evaluate_whitebox)
Calls k_spinlock_init which does not exist (implicit declaration; did you mean k_stack_init) -> undefined reference at link; onoff_manager_init should use ONOFF_MANAGER_INITIALIZER as the oracle does
monitor_unregister returns -EALREADY when the monitor is not registered; the oracle returns -EINVAL (rv init -EINVAL), and the onoff API test expects -EINVAL
release's error-state errno differs from the oracle (state-machine flags vs exact ONOFF_STATE_ERROR check); onoff_api test_error fails
request was rewritten (different ON/refs/error/RESETTING state handling and notify path vs oracle); onoff_api test_error fails
osEventFlagsDelete(NULL) returns osErrorParameter; the Zephyr portability layer returns osErrorResource for a NULL handle, so the event-flags test expecting osErrorResource fails
osEventFlagsGet(NULL) returns osFlagsErrorUnknown; the oracle returns 0 for a NULL handle (treat as no flags), so the added error return breaks the test

osKernelRestoreLock restores the lock by calling k_sched_lock()/k_sched_unlock() (count +/-1) instead of writing lock straight back into base.sched_locked as the oracle does; restoring an unlocked value can underflow sched_locked and trip an assertion -> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR (agent mislabeled as compile_error)
osKernelSysTick returns (uint32_t)k_uptime_ticks() (system ticks) instead of the oracle's k_cycle_get_32() (cycle counter), so the returned clock value is in the wrong units/scale
osMailFree passes &mail (address of the local pointer variable) to k_mem_slab_free instead of mail, freeing an invalid block -> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR (agent mislabeled as compile_error)

osMailPut replaced the oracle's non-blocking k_mbox_async_put with blocking k_mbox_put(...,K_FOREVER) and sets mmsg.size=item_sz; mailq send status semantics change, test_mailq fails expecting osErrorValue when full

osThreadCreate omits the oracle's k_poll_signal_init(thread_def->poll_signal) and k_poll_event_init(thread_def->poll_event, ...) calls before k_thread_create. The signal test (test_signal_events_isr) later uses these uninitialized poll structures, causing a segmentation fault.
Calls k_poll_signal_signal which does not exist (implicit declaration; did you mean k_poll_signal_init) -> undefined reference at link

osThreadNew omits the oracle's k_poll_signal_init() and k_poll_event_init() calls (plus tid->signal_results = 0) for the thread control block. The thread_flags test (test_thread_flags_isr) later uses these uninitialized poll structures, causing a segmentation fault.
k_timer_init called with 2 arguments while the oracle passes 3 (callback, user_data=NULL); 'too few arguments to function k_timer_init'
pm_device_is_powered returns domain_pm->state != OFF (true unless OFF) instead of the oracle's state == ACTIVE check; power-domain state semantics differ, device_power_domain test fails

pm_device_runtime_enable omits the oracle's lazy init block 'if (pm->dev == NULL) { pm->dev = dev; ... }'. As a result pm->dev stays NULL and later PM operations (during 'Cycling: test_reg_0') dereference pm->dev -> segfault. Additional deviation: also missing the pm_device_is_busy(dev) check, but that is not the direct crash trigger.
subscribe(NULL) is not handled as unregister: the model always appends and eagerly calls cb(max_latency_us) inside the lock; test_pm_policy_latency_subscribe_null_disables fails
Run ends in an uncaught kernel panic: ASSERTION FAIL [z_spin_lock_valid] invalid spinlock (the eager cb call under the latency spinlock nests a lock), so this is classified as a crash.

pm_policy_state_any_active returns true when global_lock_cnt!=0 (i.e. locked) and otherwise iterates per-state locks; the oracle returns true only when nothing is locked -> inverted logic, test_pm_policy_state_all_lock fails

When deleting a black leaf, Claude inserts an uninitialized stack-local struct rbnode null_node into the tree before calling fix_missing_black(), which then reads garbage color/child fields leading to undefined behavior and segfault. The oracle passes the still-linked real node instead. Additional deviation: uses right-subtree minimum successor instead of left-subtree maximum predecessor for the two-child case, but the null_node issue is the direct crash trigger.
ring_buf_get drops the oracle 'if (data)' guard and memcpy's unconditionally, so a NULL data pointer is dereferenced -> segfault
rtio_work_req_submit drops the !req and !iodev_sqe || !handler guards; a NULL req is dereferenced when appending -> segfault
smf_run_state clears internal state before checking terminate and reorders run/ancestor/terminate handling vs oracle; entry-terminate action count wrong
smf_set_state rewritten with different ancestor/LCA exit-action handling; exit-terminate test fails
spsc_pbuf_alloc rewritten (FREE_SPACE_DISTANCE/padding and max-len path differ from oracle); 0cpy tests fail
spsc_pbuf_claim rewritten without utilization update and with different wrap/padding handling; test_0cpy_discard fails (agent mislabeled as compile_error)
Run ends in an uncaught assert: ASSERTION FAIL [!sys_dnode_is_linked] in kernel/timeout.c during test_stress_0cpy -> crash.
spsc_pbuf_commit cache-writes only the length header (not payload) and drops the len==0 early return; spsc tests fail
spsc_pbuf_free drops the oracle PADDING_MARK / next-packet-padding handling and wraps unconditionally; 0cpy corner tests fail
spsc_pbuf_write drops the len>=SPSC_PBUF_MAX_LEN -EINVAL check and commits plen instead of len; spsc flags/util tests fail
stream_flash_init returns -EINVAL (and drops several -EFAULT size/offset/overflow checks) where the oracle validates each misalignment with -EFAULT; stream init test fails

sys_heap_init omits the oracle's 'bytes -= heap_footer_bytes(bytes)' before computing end_chunk. end_chunk is then too large, and set_chunk_size(h, end_chunk, 0) writes the end marker chunk header at mem+bytes, past the allocated heap region, corrupting adjacent memory -> segfault during test_big_heap. Additional deviations: no ROUND_UP/ROUND_DOWN on mem/end, meta_units missing CHUNK_TRAILER_SIZE, but the footer omission is the direct crash trigger.
sys_mem_blocks_get returns -EINVAL for count==0/too-large and reorders checks where the oracle returns 0/-ENOMEM via goto out; mem_block_get test fails

sys_multi_mem_blocks_free returns a non -EINVAL code (e.g. -EFAULT) when no allocator owns the block / invalid params, while the oracle returns -EINVAL; test_multi_mem_block_invalid_params expects -EINVAL and fails. Prior crash label was an artifact of a separate caught-panic test in the same binary.
usb_bos_register_cap accumulates wTotalLength from desc->bLength instead of recomputing via usb_bos_get_length() on every register; osdesc descriptor length mismatches
usb_enable rewritten (returns 0 instead of -EALREADY when already enabled, different init/vbus/ep ordering and missing descriptor-config path); device setup test fails
usb_get_device_descriptor scans for and returns the DEVICE descriptor pointer instead of the descriptor-table start the oracle returns; downstream endpoint traversal breaks

usbd_add_descriptor drops the oracle's guards for fs_desc==NULL, usbd_is_initialized(), hs_desc==NULL (if HS), and descriptor list initialization before calling desc_add_and_update_idx. This allows descriptor insertion during early init with NULL/uninitialized structures, leading to a segmentation fault right after host controller enable.
usbd_enable rewritten (preallocate/control-pipe path and lock ordering differ from oracle); control test fails
usbh_device_get_any uses SYS_DLIST_PEEK_HEAD_CONTAINER incorrectly, producing expected-expression / static-assert errors in dlist.h macros
usbh_req_setup rewritten (endpoint/transfer setup differs from oracle); control_nodata test fails
write_log_to_file skips volume check/create_log_dir and maps init failures differently (returns rc vs length); fs backend test fails
z_log_msg_commit omits msg->hdr.timestamp = timestamp_func() before commit, leaving the timestamp stale; log order test fails
Run also ends in an uncaught fatal: ASSERTION FAIL [link != NULL] in log_mgmt.c (Exiting due to fatal error) -> crash.
z_log_msg_init drops curr_log_buffer = &log_buffer under CONFIG_MPSC_PBUF, so the global stays NULL and later logging dereferences it -> segfault
z_shell_history_get reimplements up/down traversal differently (empty-list/len handling); circle-through-history test fails
z_shell_history_put compares against the tail and drops z_shell_history_mode_exit; history dedup semantics differ
zbus_chan_rm_obs manual singly-linked removal replaces the safe container iteration; removing the first runtime observer fails

zbus_init_proxy_agent lacks the oracle's _ZBUS_ASSERT checks for agent, thread_id, backend_api, thread, msgq, stack being non-NULL. In test_zbus_init_proxy_agent_invalid_params, a NULL pointer (likely agent->backend_api or agent itself) is dereferenced, causing a segmentation fault. Additionally, initialization order is changed (backend_init before thread creation/set_recv_cb), but the missing NULL guards are the direct crash trigger.
linear_range_get_index returns 0 for step==0 before performing the range checks, so out-of-range values that should return -ERANGE succeed; get_index test fails
linear_range_get_win_index changed step==0 handling/early returns vs oracle; window index test fails
ring_buf_is_empty now calls ring_buf_size_get declared later -> implicit declaration and conflicting-types errors in ring_buffer.h
ring_buf_size_get returns put.head - get.tail instead of the oracle put.tail - get.head (free vs used space), breaking ring buffer byte tests
ring_buf_space_get calls ring_buf_size_get before it is declared -> implicit declaration / conflicting types in ring_buffer.h
spsc_pbuf_capacity returns pb->common.len instead of len - sizeof(uint32_t) (header slot not reserved), capacity is 4 bytes too large; 0cpy test fails
timespec_from_timeout drops the K_FOREVER/K_NO_WAIT handling and only asserts relative timeouts, so an absolute/forever timeout trips the assert -> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR (mislabeled compile_error)

Claude replaced the oracle's _ZBUS_ASSERT with Zephyr's __ASSERT for NULL checks. In test_specification_based__zbus_obs_set_enable with obs==NULL, __ASSERT triggers a fatal kernel panic (ASSERTION FAIL at zbus.h:1146) while the oracle's _ZBUS_ASSERT does not abort in this configuration. The function body is otherwise identical; the macro choice is the sole behavioral difference causing the crash.
